body: A new technique has let the company probe deeper than ever into the weird workings of an LLM.

The AI firm Anthropic has developed a technique that has given it the clearest glimpse yet at what’s really going on inside large language models as they answer questions or carry out tasks. What they found ranges from the mundane to the unnerving.

Researchers at the company built a tool called the Jacobian lens (or J-lens) and used it to uncover a hidden area, which they named the J-space, inside Claude Opus 4.6, a version of Anthropic’s flagship LLM released in February.

The J-space contains individual words that are related to the words and phrases that the model is most likely to spit out in a response in the near future. If Claude were a person (which it is not), you might say that these hidden words can reveal what’s on its mind before it actually speaks.

Anthropic found that what an LLM is actually doing can often be different from what it says it is doing. The company claims that monitoring words that pop up in the J-space gives it a new way to understand and control its models.

The company shared its results in a paper posted on its website this week. It has also teamed up with Neuronpedia, an open-source platform that lets you poke around inside LLMs yourself, to make a hands-on demo that anyone can try.
“It’s very good and interesting work,” says Tom McGrath, chief scientist and cofounder at Goodfire, a startup that also builds tools to understand and control LLMs .

For the last couple of years, Anthropic has been pushing the envelope in a field of research known as mechanistic interpretability, which involves probing the internal workings of LLMs to see how they tick . ( MIT Technology Review picked mechanistic interpretability as one of this year’s top breakthrough technologies.) The new technique builds on previous work from Anthropic and others to expose a deeper level inside LLMs that researchers had not seen before.

Picture an LLM as a stack of books. Each book is a layer of basic computational units known as neurons, with each neuron in one layer passing information to the neurons in the layers above. The books at the bottom of the stack are the input layers, which process the text coming into the model. The books at the top are the output layers, which prepare the text that the model is about to produce. Much of what goes on in these input and output layers is housekeeping.

But in the middle of the stack, you get the layers that do the heavy lifting, churning through the complex math that turns prompts into responses one word at a time. That’s where the really clever—and mysterious—stuff happens.

To peer deeper into those middle layers, Anthropic adapted an existing tool called a logit lens. A logit lens can be used to look inside an LLM to identify the words that it is likely to produce next. Moving the lens down the stack of books reveals what words the LLM is focusing on at that particular point in its number crunching.

Anthropic’s J-lens works in a similar way but picks out words that an LLM is likely to say at some point in the near future, not necessarily straight away. What that reveals in practice are words that are related to the response an LLM is working on but that might not actually end up being part of that response by the time the math in the middle layers has run its course.

paragraphTranslations: 一项新技术让该公司比以往任何时候都能更深入地探索大型语言模型（LLM）的奇异运作。
人工智能公司Anthropic开发了一种技术，使其能够最清晰地窥视大型语言模型在回答问题或执行任务时内部真正发生的事情。他们的发现从平凡到令人不安都有。
该公司的研究人员构建了一个名为Jacobian镜头（或J镜头）的工具，并用它来揭示一个隐藏区域，他们将其命名为J空间，这是Anthropic旗舰LLM的一个版本，名为Claude Opus 4.6，于今年二月发布。
J空间包含与模型在不久的将来最有可能在回应中吐出的单词和短语相关的单个单词。如果Claude是一个人（它不是），你可能会说这些隐藏的单词可以揭示它在实际说话之前在想什么。
Anthropic发现LLM实际在做的事情常常与它所说的它正在做的事情不同。该公司声称，监控J空间中出现的单词为其提供了一种新的方式来理解和控制其模型。
该公司本周在其网站上发布的一篇论文中分享了其结果。它还与Neuronpedia合作，Neuronpedia是一个开源平台，让你可以亲自探索LLM内部，制作了一个任何人都可以尝试的动手演示。
“这是非常好且有趣的工作，”Goodfire的首席科学家和联合创始人Tom McGrath说，Goodfire是一家也构建工具以理解和控制LLM的初创公司。
在过去的几年里，Anthropic一直在推动一个名为机制可解释性的研究领域的边界，该领域涉及探索LLM的内部运作，看看它们是如何运作的。（MIT Technology Review将机制可解释性选为今年顶级突破技术之一）。这项新技术基于Anthropic和其他人之前的工作，揭示了研究人员以前未曾见过的LLM内部更深层次。
将LLM想象成一堆书。每本书是一个由称为神经元的基本计算单元组成的层，每个层中的每个神经元都将信息传递给上层的神经元。堆叠底部的书是输入层，它们处理进入模型的文本。顶部的书是输出层，它们准备模型即将产生的文本。这些输入和输出层中的大部分活动都是例行公事。
但在堆叠的中间，你得到了承担重任的层，它们通过复杂的数学将提示逐字转换成回应。那就是真正聪明——和神秘——的事情所在。
为了更深入地窥视这些中间层，Anthropic改进了一个名为logit镜头的现有工具。logit镜头可以用来查看LLM内部，以识别它接下来可能产生的单词。将镜头沿着书堆移动，可以揭示LLM在数字计算的特定时刻所关注的单词。
Anthropic的J镜头的工作方式类似，但挑选出LLM在不久的将来某个时候可能会说出的单词，而不一定是立即。在实践中，这揭示了与LLM正在处理的回应相关的单词，但当中间层的数学运算完成时，这些单词可能实际上并不构成该回应的一部分。

articles.title: OpenAI launches its new family of models with GPT-5.6
articles.subtitle: OpenAI's latest family of models promise improvements across a range of areas, including cybersecurity.
articles.author: Lucas Ropek
articles.summary: OpenAI's latest family of models promise improvements across a range of areas, including cybersecurity.
body: OpenAI unveiled its newest family of models on Thursday, introducing a new set of heavyweight programs into an increasingly crowded field of AI offerings.

GPT-5.6 comes in three variants: Sol (considered its workhorse), Terra (a more intermediate option), and Luna (its budget friendly option). These models expand what users can do across a variety of fields — with the company promising powerful capabilities in enterprise work, coding, and even scientific research.

CEO Sam Altman has promised that his company’s newest models are orders of magnitude more efficient and cost-effective than previous versions, recently telling CNBC that Sol is 54% more token efficient when it comes to AI coding tasks.
Most notably, the company calls 5.6 its “strongest cybersecurity model yet, achieving frontier performance with significantly fewer tokens.”

Indeed, much hubbub has been made about the model’s cyber capabilities, as the Trump administration previously sought to restrict its rollout , ostensibly due to fears of how the model could be misused. GPT-5.6 supports defensive activities, including threat modeling, code review and patching, and blue teaming (simulating an attack on your own systems to find weaknesses before real hackers do).

OpenAI also released a new tool called ChatGPT Work , which — just as it sounds — is designed as a workplace companion for enterprise teams, running on desktop, web, and mobile, that can help with daily clerical tasks, like drafting documents, spreadsheets, and presentations.
OpenAI’s newly announced family of models follows on the heels of similar releases this week from competitors SpaceXAI and Meta.

However, GPT-5.6 and its attendant marketing seems most designed to take aim at OpenAI’s primary opponent, Anthropic. Anthropic has managed to make itself the likable underdog of the AI race, focusing fixedly on enterprise customers and winning a growing share of support as a result.
Not to be outdone, OpenAI cites the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index , a notable benchmarking metric, to claim that its latest family of models outshines Anthropic’s models at every turn.

OpenAI calls Sol its “best coding model yet,” and has explicitly compared it to Anthropic’s recently released (and much hyped) Fable . Using the Coding Agent Index, OpenAI claims that Sol “sets a new state of the art at 80, 2.8 points above Fable 5, while using less than half the output tokens, taking less than half the time, and costing about one-third less.”
It adds: “That advantage extends across the family: Terra performs just above Fable 5, while Luna outperforms Opus 4.8.”

The company says that 5.6 is now available across ChatGPT, Codex, and the OpenAI API. Availability per million tokens is priced as follows: Sol is $5 input / $30 output, Terra is $2.50 input / $15 output, and Luna is $1 input / $6 output.

GPT-5.6 comes in three variants: Sol (considered its workhorse), Terra (a more intermediate option), and Luna (its budget friendly option). These models expand what users can do across a variety of fields — with the company promising powerful capabilities in enterprise work, coding, and even scientific research.

CEO Sam Altman has promised that his company’s newest models are orders of magnitude more efficient and cost-effective than previous versions, recently telling CNBC that Sol is 54% more token efficient when it comes to AI coding tasks.
paragraphTranslations: OpenAI周四发布了其最新的模型系列，将一套新的重量级程序引入了日益拥挤的人工智能产品领域。
GPT-5.6有三个变体：Sol（被认为是其主力军），Terra（一个更中级的选项）和Luna（其预算友好的选项）。这些模型扩展了用户在各个领域能做的事情——公司承诺在企业工作、编程甚至科学研究方面具有强大的能力。
首席执行官Sam Altman承诺，他公司的最新款模型比以往版本更高效、更具成本效益，最近告诉CNBC，Sol在AI编码任务中比之前版本节省了54%的代币。
最值得注意的是，公司称5.6是其“迄今为止最强的网络安全模型，以显著更少的代币实现了前沿性能。”
确实，关于该模型的网络能力有很多讨论，因为特朗普政府之前曾试图限制其推出，表面上是因为担心该模型可能被滥用。GPT-5.6支持防御活动，包括威胁建模、代码审查和修补，以及蓝队行动（模拟对您自己系统的攻击，以在真正的黑客之前找到弱点）。
OpenAI还发布了一个名为ChatGPT Work的新工具，正如其名称所暗示的，它被设计为企业团队的工作场所伴侣，运行在桌面、网络和移动设备上，可以帮助处理日常的文书工作，如起草文件、电子表格和演示文稿。
OpenAI新宣布的模型系列紧随竞争对手SpaceXAI和Meta本周的类似发布之后。
然而，GPT-5.6及其伴随的市场推广似乎最针对OpenAI的主要对手Anthropic。Anthropic成功地将自己定位为AI竞赛中的可爱弱者，专注于企业客户，并因此赢得了越来越多的支持。
不甘示弱，OpenAI引用了人工分析编码代理指数，这是一个值得注意的基准指标，声称其最新的模型系列在每个方面都超越了Anthropic的模型。
OpenAI称Sol为其“迄今为止最好的编码模型”，并明确将其与Anthropic最近发布（且备受炒作）的Fable进行了比较。使用编码代理指数，OpenAI声称Sol“在80个点上设定了新的艺术状态，比Fable 5高出2.8点，同时使用的输出代币不到一半，所需时间不到一半，成本大约降低了三分之一。”
它补充道：“这一优势贯穿整个家族：Terra的性能略高于Fable 5，而Luna的性能超过了Opus 4.8。”
公司表示，5.6现在可以在ChatGPT、Codex和OpenAI API中使用。每百万代币的可用性定价如下：Sol是5美元输入/30美元输出，Terra是2.50美元输入/15美元输出，Luna是1美元输入/6美元输出。
